sentences.text: Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 20.

To prove the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, on his treatment, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1, by way of evidence affidavit Ex.PW1/A, wherein he deposed that he has already filed all his treatment papers and bills, with the DAR proceedings and in his evidence, he has placed reliance upon the DAR as Ex.PW1/1 (Colly).

However, perusal of DAR reveals that IO mentioned that the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs. 3,310/- but, he has not given his bills to him and the petitioner told the IO, that he will file his bills, directly in the court.
Thus, the IO has only placed on record, copy of medical treatment record of the petitioner, along with photocopy of medical bills.

But, as the petitioner has not filed any original medical bills therefore, in the absence of original medical bills, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation, under the head of medical expenses.

they failed to elicit any admissions, so as to prove that the accident has not taken place, due to involvement of the offending vehicle or due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

that the accident, in which PW1 has sustained injuries, has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
